ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the output-input characteristic curve of the hysteresis voltage comparator shown in the figure, when \(u_i > +3V\), the output voltage \(u_o\) = ________ V.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure shows the output-input characteristic curve of a hysteresis voltage comparator, with the horizontal axis labeled u_i and the vertical axis labeled u_o. The upper horizontal segment of the curve is labeled +5V, and the lower horizontal segment is labeled -5V; there are vertical jumping segments at u_i = -3V and u_i = +3V, among which the vertical segment at +3V jumps downward from +5V to -5V. Then reason: the problem gives u_i > +3V, that is, on the right side of the +3V mark on the horizontal axis. According to the branch after the downward jump at +3V in the figure, the right side corresponds to the lower horizontal line, and the output voltage is -5V.

method.method_draft: First describe the graph: it shows a hysteresis comparator characteristic with levels +5 V and -5 V, and switching points at -3 V and +3 V. From the text, locate the condition u_i > +3 V on the horizontal axis, i.e., to the right of the +3 V mark. On the plotted loop, after the vertical drop at +3 V, the branch for larger u_i is the bottom horizontal line labeled -5 V. Therefore read u_o as -5 V.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: the characteristic has an upper threshold at +3 V where the arrow indicates a downward jump from the +5 V level to the -5 V level. The text asks for u_o when u_i > +3 V. Apply the hysteresis rule: once the input exceeds the upper threshold, the comparator switches into the low saturation state and stays on that branch for still larger input. The low saturation level marked in the figure is -5 V, so u_o = -5 V.
